def: to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in

occurrences.text: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.
And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
